mainEntity.name: How do I calculate miles per gallon?

acceptedAnswer.text: Divide the miles you drove by the gallons of fuel you used. If you drove 340 miles and added 11.93 gallons at the next full fill-up, your fuel economy is 340 ÷ 11.93 = 28.5 MPG.

mainEntity.name: How do I convert MPG to L/100 km?

acceptedAnswer.text: Divide 235.215 by the US MPG figure. For example, 28.5 MPG is 8.25 L/100 km. The same formula converts back: MPG = 235.215 ÷ L/100 km. UK gallons are larger, so UK MPG uses 282.481.

mainEntity.name: How is the carbon emission worked out?

acceptedAnswer.text: The EPA gives 8,887 grams (8.887 kg) of CO₂ for each gallon of gasoline burned. Multiply gallons used by that factor for the tailpipe CO₂ of the trip. It does not include emissions from producing the fuel.

mainEntity.name: How does the EV comparison work?

acceptedAnswer.text: Enter miles per kWh (many EVs manage 3 to 4) and your electricity price. Trip miles divided by miles per kWh gives kWh used, and multiplying by the price gives the charging cost. Public fast chargers cost more than home charging.

mainEntity.name: Why is my MPG lower in winter?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cold engines run richer, cold air is denser, tires lose pressure, and winter fuel blends and heating use energy. Short trips make it worse because the engine spends more time warming up.
